Rashi on Yevamot 12a:11:1.hebrew: מיאנה בבעל - קטנה יתומה נכרית שמיאנה בבעל מותרת לחמיה, לפי שעקרתה לקדושין, והרי היא כמפותה, ולא כלתו היא:
Rashi on Yevamot 12a:11:1.english: Refused [her] husband - An unrelated orphaned minor girl who refused [her] husband is permitted to her father-in-law, because she uproots the betrothal, and behold, she is like a seduced woman, and she is not his daughter-in-law.

Rashi on Yevamot 12a:11:2.hebrew: ביבם אסורה לאביו - דכיון דאהנו נישואין קמאי לזקקה ליבם, נראית כאשתו גמורה ונראית ככלתו של זה:
Rashi on Yevamot 12a:11:2.english: [If she refused] the yavam, she is forbidden to his father - For since the first marriage was effective in binding her to the yavam, she appears like his full-fledged wife and appears like this [father]'s daughter-in-law.

Rashi on Yevamot 12a:13:1.english: Here, too - [In the case of] his daughter who performed refusal.

Rashi on Yevamot 12a:13:2.hebrew: משעת נפילה - שנפלה בתו לפניו לייבום והוצרכה למאן בו, נראית כאשת אחיו, ונראית צרתה צרת הבת:
Rashi on Yevamot 12a:13:2.english: From the time of falling [for levirate marriage] - When his daughter fell before him for levirate marriage and needed to refuse him, she appears like his brother's wife, and her rival wife appears [to be] the rival wife of the daughter.

Rashi on Yevamot 12a:14:1.hebrew: צרת אילונית - הרי שהיה נשוי ב' נשים, והא' אילונית. אילונית — דוכרניתא דלא ילדה, לשון איל, זכר מן הצאן:
Rashi on Yevamot 12a:14:1.english: The rival wife of an aylonit - Suppose [a man] was married to two women, and one [of them] was an aylonit. Aylonit [means] masculine [in nature], who does not give birth — [from] the term ayil [ram], a male of the flock.

Rashi on Yevamot 12a:14:2.english: And he died without children - Both of them are forbidden to enter into levirate marriage and are exempt from chalitzah.

Rashi on Yevamot 12a:14:3.hebrew: שנאמר והיה הבכור אשר תלד בראויה לילד פרט לאילונית - וכיון דפטורה, קיימא עליה באשת אח, וצרתה צרת ערוה. ואע"ג דהאי והיה הבכור אשר תלד מיתוקם במכילתין לקמן (יבמות דף כד.) בגדול האחים, ומהכא נפקא לן מצוה בגדול לייבם, מ"מ דרשינן הך פרט לאילונית מאשר תלד, דקרא יתירא הוא, כיון דהבכור ביבם גופיה משתעי:
Rashi on Yevamot 12a:14:3.english: As it is stated: "And the firstborn that she bears" — [referring to] one who is fit to bear [children], to the exclusion of an aylonit - And since she is exempt [from levirate marriage], she remains [forbidden] to him as a brother's wife, and her rival wife is the rival wife of a forbidden relative. And even though this [verse], "And the firstborn that she bears," is established later in our tractate (Yevamot 24a) [as referring] to the eldest of the brothers — and from here we derive [that] it is a mitzvah for the eldest to perform levirate marriage — nevertheless, we expound this exclusion of an aylonit from "that she bears," for it is a superfluous [phrase in the] verse, since "the firstborn" speaks of the yavam himself.

Rashi on Yevamot 12a:16:1.hebrew: דכתיב ומת אחד מהם - ולא זו שמתו ב' בעליה וזיקת שניהם עליה, ושתיהן אסורות מדרבנן, וקרא אסמכתא בעלמא כדמפרש בפ' ד' אחין. ובחליצה דחדא לא מיפטרא אידך, דלאו מבית אחד קאתו הואיל ולא כנסה. ואי לא עבד בה מאמר, לא הואי עלה אלא זיקת ראשון, והוו להו שתי יבמות הבאות מב' בתים, ושתיהן מתייבמות:
Rashi on Yevamot 12a:16:1.english: For it is written: "And one of them dies" - And not this [woman] whose two husbands died and the [levirate] bond of both of them is upon her. And both of them [the two widows] are forbidden [for levirate marriage] by rabbinic decree, and the verse is merely a scriptural support [asmakhta], as is explained in the chapter [entitled] Arba'ah Achin [Four Brothers]. And through the chalitzah of one, the other is not exempted, since they do not come from one house inasmuch as he did not consummate the marriage with her. And if he had not performed ma'amar [levirate betrothal] with her, there would only be upon her the [levirate] bond of the first [brother], and they would be two yevamot coming from two houses, and both of them would enter into levirate marriage.

Rashi on Yevamot 12a:16:2.english: Behold, these - [referring to the] two wives.

Rashi on Yevamot 12a:16:3.hebrew: חולצות - דאילו כנסה, הוה פקעה זיקה קמייתא ולא הוה עלה אלא זיקת נשואי האחרון; אבל מאמר לא מפקע זיקה, והויא עלה קצת זיקת ראשון וקצת זיקת האחרון:
Rashi on Yevamot 12a:16:3.english: Perform ḥalitza - For had he consummated the marriage with her, the first [levirate] bond would have dissolved, and she would be subject only to the [levirate] bond of the marriage of the latter [brother]; however, ma'amar [levirate betrothal] does not dissolve a [levirate] bond, and [thus] she is subject to part of the first [brother's] bond and part of the latter [brother's] bond.

Rashi on Yevamot 12a:17:1.hebrew: שאיסור נפילה גרם לה - שנפלה ב' פעמים מזיקה אחת:
Rashi on Yevamot 12a:17:1.english: For whom the prohibition of falling [before the yavam] caused her [to be forbidden] - For she fell [before the yavam] two times from a single levirate bond.

Rashi on Yevamot 12a:17:2.hebrew: שלא מצינו בכל התורה - שתאסר, אלא מדרבנן הוא דמיתסרא, שאין כאן איסור ערוה, ואסורה צרתה:
Rashi on Yevamot 12a:17:2.english: We have not found in the entire Torah - that she would be forbidden [by Torah law]; rather, it is by rabbinic decree that she is forbidden, for there is no prohibition of ervah here, and [yet] her rival wife is forbidden.

Rashi on Yevamot 12a:19:1.hebrew: הא דאורייתא - "תלד", למעוטי צרת אילונית, דאסירא ואפילו חליצה לא בעיא:
Rashi on Yevamot 12a:19:1.english: This [one is] by Torah law - [From the verse, "whom] she shall bear" [Deut. 25:6], to exclude the rival wife of an aylonit, who is forbidden [to the yavam] and does not even require ḥalitza.

Rashi on Yevamot 12a:19:2.hebrew: והא דרבנן - כדמפרש טעמא בפ' ד' אחין, וקאסרי לה על השלישי:
Rashi on Yevamot 12a:19:2.english: And this [is] by rabbinic [law] - As [the Gemara] explains the reason in the chapter [entitled] Arba'ah Achim, and [the Sages] forbid her to the third [brother].

Rashi on Yevamot 12a:1:1.hebrew: א"ל תניתוה - אתרווייהו לישני מהדר, דקתני אחת כשרה ואחת פסולה, אלמא היא אסורה וצרתה מותרת:
Rashi on Yevamot 12a:1:1.english: He said to him: We learned it - He is responding to both versions [of the discussion], for it teaches: "one [was] fit and one [was] disqualified" — thus, she is forbidden [for levirate marriage], and her rival wife is permitted.

Rashi on Yevamot 12a:20:1.hebrew: כאן שהכיר בה - דרב אסי בשהכיר בה כשנשאה שהיא אילונית, ואין כאן מקח טעות, והרי היא אשתו, וצרתה הויא צרת אילונית, ורחמנא פטרה מאשר תלד. ומתני' — בשלא הכיר בה כשנשאה שתהא אילונית, ומקחו מקח טעות, ולאו אשתו היא; לפיכך צרתה מותרת, דלאו צרת אילונית היא:
Rashi on Yevamot 12a:20:1.english: Here, [where] he knew about her - [The statement] of Rav Asi [refers to a case] where he knew about her when he married her that she was an aylonit, so there is no mistaken transaction here, and behold, she is his wife, and her rival wife is the rival wife of an aylonit, whom the Merciful One exempted [from levirate marriage] by [the verse] "whom she shall bear." And [our] Mishnah [refers to a case] where he did not know about her when he married her that she was an aylonit, so his acquisition is a mistaken transaction, and she is not his wife; therefore, her rival wife is permitted, for she is not the rival wife of an aylonit.

Rashi on Yevamot 12a:5:1.hebrew: צרת ממאנת - נפלו לפניו ב' יבמות מאח אחד — גדולה וקטנה — ומיאנה בו הקטנה, צרתה אסורה:
Rashi on Yevamot 12a:5:1.english: The rival wife of [a minor] who performed refusal - Two yevamot fell before him from one [deceased] brother — an adult and a minor — and the minor refused him; her rival wife is forbidden.

Rashi on Yevamot 12a:5:2.hebrew: למאן - אסורה? אילימא אף לשאר אחין, השתא היא גופה מותרת לזה:
Rashi on Yevamot 12a:5:2.english: To whom - [is she] forbidden? If we say even to the other brothers — now, if she herself is permitted to this [brother], [could her rival wife be forbidden]?

Rashi on Yevamot 12a:6:1.hebrew: אלא לדידיה - ליבם שמיאנה בו אסורה, דמיאון עקר ליה לזיקה וקאי עליה באשת אח. וא"ת: מיאון נישואין קמאי עקר, והרי היא נכרית אצלו ומותרת לו? גזירה דרבנן היא: הואיל ולא מיאנה בראשון ומכח נישואין נפלה להתייבם, נראית כאשת אחיו; והכי אמרי' לקמן: משעת נפילה נראית ככלתו כו'. והא דשמואל בפ' ב"ש (לקמן יבמות דף קז:):
Rashi on Yevamot 12a:6:1.english: Rather, to him - She is forbidden to the brother-in-law whom she refused, because refusal uproots the levirate bond, and she stands [prohibited] to him as a brother's wife. And if you say: refusal uproots the first marriage [retroactively], so behold she is a stranger to him and should be permitted to him? It is a rabbinic decree: since she did not refuse the first [husband] and fell [before him] for levirate marriage by virtue of [that] marriage, she appears like his brother's wife; and so we say later on: "From the time she falls [for levirate marriage], she appears like his daughter-in-law," etc. And this [statement] of Shmuel is in the chapter [entitled] Beit Shammai (later, Yevamot 107b).

Rashi on Yevamot 12a:7:1.hebrew: משום צרת בתו ממאנת - דאתי למישרי צרת בתו קטנה שנפלה לו לייבום ומיאנה בו, דאמרינן: נישואין קמאי קא עקרא, ואין זו צרת ערוה. וה"ד מיאון בבתו הואיל והוא קיים, דאין מיאון אלא ביתומה שלא קיבל אביה קידושיה? משכחת לה ביתומה בחיי האב, כדתנן בפרק ב"ש: קטנה שהשיאה אביה ונתגרשה — הרי היא יתומה בחיי האב, דפקע לה זכותיה מינה משיצתה מרשותו; ואם הלכה ונשאת לאחי אביה, יכולה למאן ביבם בחיי אביה:
Rashi on Yevamot 12a:7:1.english: Due to [the case of] a rival wife of his daughter who performed refusal - For one might come to permit the rival wife of his minor daughter who fell before him for levirate marriage and performed refusal against him, since we say she uproots the first marriage, and this [other woman] is not the rival wife of a forbidden relative. And how can refusal occur with his daughter while he is alive, given that refusal applies only to an orphan girl whose father did not accept her betrothal? You find it in [the case of] an orphan in her father's lifetime, as we learned in the chapter [entitled] Beit Shammai: A minor girl whose father married her off and she was divorced — behold, she is an orphan in her father's lifetime, for his authority over her ceased once she left his domain; and if she went and married her father's brother, she can perform refusal against the levir during her father's lifetime.

Tosafot on Yevamot 12a:18:1.hebrew: מאי לאו למעוטי צרת אילונית דשריא - וא"ת: אמאי לא פריך מינה לעיל למאן דאסר צרת מחזיר גרושתו, ולימא ליה: "מאי לאו למעוטי צרת מחזיר גרושתו דשרי"? וי"ל: דלא משמע ליה למעוטי מ"זו היא" אלא כיוצא בה; דאילונית דמיא לאשת שני מתים, דזו וזו מותרות לבעליהן, אבל מחזיר גרושתו נאסרה לבעלה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 12a:18:1.english: What, [is it] not to exclude the rival wife of an aylonit, that she is permitted? - And if you will ask: Why did [the Gemara] not raise an objection from it above against the one who forbids the rival wife of one who remarries his divorcee, and say to him: "What, [is it] not to exclude the rival wife of one who remarries his divorcee, that she is permitted?" And one can answer: For it does not seem [to the Gemara] to exclude from "This is" anything other than [a case] similar to it; for an aylonit is similar to the wife of two deceased [brothers], as both this one and that one are permitted to their husbands, whereas one who remarries his divorcee was forbidden to her husband.

Tosafot on Yevamot 12a:22:1.hebrew: תני שהיו - וא"ת: לרבא, דשרי צרת בתו אילונית אפי' הכיר בה — מה חידוש הוא לשנות בתוספתא: "וכולן שנמצאו אילונית, בין בחיי הבעל בין לאחר מיתה"? בשלמא לרב אסי, איצטריך לאשמועינן בחיי בעל, דסד"א הואיל ובחייו נמצאת אילונית, דלמא קיבלה. וי"ל, דס"ד למיסרה כשנמצאת אחר מיתה, משום דבשעת נפילה נראית כצרת בתו, כדאסר לעיל צרת בתו ממאנת. וא"ת: מ"ש אילונית הממאנת? ויש לומר: דהתם מיחסרא מיאון, הכא לא מיחסרא מידי. א"נ, ממאנת אין לה קול, ובשעת מיאון נראית כצרת בתו; אבל אילונית יש לה קול, וידוע שלא היתה צרת בתו. וא"ת: מאי פריך הכא לרבא מדקתני "שנמצאו", נימא דנקט "נמצאו" לרבותא? וי"ל, דבהכיר בה איכא רבותא טפי; להכי משני: "תני שהיו":
Tosafot on Yevamot 12a:22:1.english: Teach: "That were [an aylonit]" - And if you ask: According to Rava, who permits the rival wife of his daughter who is an aylonit even if [the husband] recognized her [condition], what novelty is there in teaching in the Tosefta: "And all of them who were found [to be] an aylonit, whether during the husband's lifetime or after [his] death"? It is understandable according to Rav Asi: it was necessary to teach us [the case] during the husband's lifetime, for you might have thought that since she was found [to be] an aylonit during his lifetime, perhaps he accepted her. And one can answer: [According to Rava, too, it is needed, because] you might have thought to forbid her when she is found [to be an aylonit] after [his] death, since at the time of falling [for levirate marriage] she appears like the rival wife of his daughter, just as [the Gemara] forbade above the rival wife of his daughter who refuses [her husband]. And if you ask: What is the difference between an aylonit and one who refuses? And one can answer: There [in the case of refusal], she lacks [an act of] refusal; here [in the case of an aylonit], she does not lack anything. Alternatively: One who refuses has no publicity, and at the time of refusal she appears like the rival wife of his daughter; but an aylonit has publicity, and it is known that she was never the rival wife of his daughter. And if you ask: What does [the Gemara] ask here against Rava from [the fact] that it teaches "who were found" — let us say that it stated "were found" to convey a greater novelty? And one can answer: In [the case of] "he recognized her," there is a greater novelty; therefore [the Gemara] answers: "Teach: 'that were.'"

Tosafot on Yevamot 12a:6:1.hebrew: צרתה נמי לא עבדה ביה מעשה - תימה: נהי דלא עבדה ביה מעשה, מ"מ כיון דהממאנת אסורה ליה, הוי צרתה כצרת ערוה, והיכי מדמה לה לממאנת דשריא לאחין:
Tosafot on Yevamot 12a:6:1.english: Her rival wife also did not perform an act with him - This is puzzling: Granted that she did not perform an act [of refusal] with him, nevertheless, since the one who performed refusal is forbidden to him, her rival wife is like the rival wife of an ervah [forbidden relative], so how can [the Gemara] compare her to the one who performed refusal, who is permitted to the [other] brothers?

Tosafot on Yevamot 12a:8:1.hebrew: אלא לאו ביבם וקתני צרותיהן מותרות - שהמיאון עוקר לנישואין קמאי. תימה: למאי דס"ד השתא, תקשה ליה סיפא דקתני "כל שיכולה למאן ולא מיאנה, צרתה חולצת ולא מתייבמת" — ואם איתא דעקרה נישואין קמאי, תמאן השתא ותתייבם צרתה, דהכי פריך עלה לקמן. וי"ל: דלמאי דסלקא דעתך השתא מצי למימר דמתני' בדליתא קמן שתמאן, או בגדולה; ולקמן דפריך עלה, משום דבעי לאוקמי מתני' אפילו היא קטנה ואיתה קמן:
Tosafot on Yevamot 12a:8:1.english: "Rather, is it not [referring to a case where she refused] the yavam?" And [the Mishnah] teaches, "Their rival wives are permitted" - because refusal uproots the original marriage. [This is] puzzling: according to what we currently assume, the latter clause [of the Mishnah] should pose a difficulty for it, as it teaches, "Any [minor] who could have refused and did not refuse, her rival wife performs chalitzah and does not enter into levirate marriage" — and if it is true that [refusal] uproots the original marriage, let her refuse now and her rival wife may enter into levirate marriage, for indeed [the Gemara] raises this objection against it below. One can answer that according to what we currently assume, one could say that the Mishnah [is dealing with a case] where she is not before us to refuse, or where she is an adult; and below, when [the Gemara] raises this objection against it, it is because it wants to establish the Mishnah [as referring] even [to a case where] she is a minor and is before us.
